notes: The 1963 volume of the Recreation and Park Commission. Curated: design approvals and gifts of plans, architects' contracts and the Palace of Fine Arts restoration bid.

findings.description: The Recreation and Park Commission accepted the Strybing Arboretum Society's gift of an information kiosk for the arboretum, worth about $3,000, and approved its drawing by Gardner A. Dailey and Associates.

findings.address_as_written: Sash enclosure of the Merry-go-round at the Childrens Quarters, Golden Gate Park
findings.description: The Recreation and Park Commission referred Schubart and Friedman's plans for enclosing the merry-go-round at the Children's Quarters with sash to its committee and staff, asking that the panels be of Plexiglass as far as possible and divided small against breakage; it had approved the architects' agreement for the enclosure, repairs and painting in February (Resolution 5173).

findings.description: The Recreation and Park Commission made the first payment, $7,830, to Lawrence Halprin & Associates, John S. Bolles and Mario J. Ciampi, appointed as consultants to prepare schematic plans for the 4.04-acre Ferry Building Park.

findings.description: The Director of Public Works told the Recreation and Park Commission that the low bid for restoring the Palace of Fine Arts under the Cahill Plan, from Frank Modglin, was $6,600,000, $1,600,000 more than the money available; the Commission let the Mayor's study committee explore the alternatives, among them John Cahill's suggestion to leave out the urns and part of the colonnades for later.
